run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: Read-only query results for the three app-280 log indices, sampled inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T06:58:04Z to 2026-11-21T06:58:04Z. (1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: the requested term {level:"ERROR"} returned 0, and the index mapping has no 'level' field at all - its fields are @timestamp(date), message(text), service(keyword) and severity(keyword), so 'severity' is the right severity field. Re-running term {severity:"ERROR"} still returned 0, and a match_all over the entire authorized window also returned 0 documents even though the index holds 16 documents, so no document of index a was observable inside the window and its ERROR count in-window is 0 while the whole-index count is unknown. (2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3: the requested terms {level:["ERROR","FATAL"]} returned 0; this index maps no 'level' field - severity is the integer field severity_num. Document contents show the encoding is non-standard: severity_num 5 carries "[ERROR]" messages (6 docs), 6 carries "[FATAL]" (2 docs) and 3 carries "[INFO]" (5 docs), so the correct severity query is terms {severity_num:[5,6]}, which returned 8. (3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3: the requested range on @timestamp plus level=ERROR returned 0 because the index maps no date field and no @timestamp at all - its fields are ingest_ts(keyword), level(keyword) and message(text), so the tool applied no time filter. Using ingest_ts (ISO-like strings without timezone) with a lexicographic range for today 2026-11-21 plus level=ERROR returned 7; the whole index holds 12 ERROR and 4 INFO of 16 documents. All counts are exact hits from index-scoped searches; index a's documents and index c's document timestamps could not be tied to the authorized window.

claims.text: In index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 the query {"term":{"level":"ERROR"}} returned total 0 (relation eq), because that index does not map a 'level' field.

The mapping of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has exactly four fields: @timestamp(date), message(text), service(keyword) and severity(keyword); the correctly named severity field for this index is 'severity'.
Searching app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 with {"term":{"severity":"ERROR"}} over the full authorized window returned total 0.

A match_all search against app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 over 2026-11-20T06:58:04Z-2026-11-21T06:58:04Z returned total 0 documents and empty severity and service aggregation buckets, while the index's document count is 16.
In index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 the query {"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}} returned total 0, because that index maps no 'level' field.
The mapping of app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 has four fields: @timestamp(date), msg(text), severity_num(integer) and svc(keyword), so severity for this index is the integer field severity_num.

The 13 documents of app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned for 2026-11-20T06:58:04Z-2026-11-21T06:58:04Z show severity_num 5 on messages '[ERROR] DB timeout 1..6' (6 docs), severity_num 6 on '[FATAL] Disk full 1..2' (2 docs) and severity_num 3 on '[INFO] healthcheck 1..5' (5 docs), all with svc order-280.
In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 the severity field distribution over the authorized window is severity_num 5 = 6 docs, 3 = 5 docs, 6 = 2 docs (total 13).
Re-running the severity query against app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 as {"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}} over 2026-11-20T06:58:04Z-2026-11-21T06:58:04Z returned total 8 (6 ERROR + 2 FATAL).
The requested range on @timestamp combined with level=ERROR in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0, because that index maps no date field and no @timestamp field.
The mapping of app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has three fields: ingest_ts(keyword), level(keyword) and message(text); there is no date-typed field, so the correct time field is the keyword ingest_ts.

All 16 documents of app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 carry ingest_ts as timezone-less ISO-like strings ranging from '2026-11-20T08:01:00' to '2026-11-21T09:04:00'; the level distribution of the index is ERROR = 12 docs and INFO = 4 docs.
Re-running on the correct time field, {"range":{"ingest_ts":{"gte":"2026-11-21T00:00:00","lte":"2026-11-21T23:59:59"}}} plus {"term":{"level":"ERROR"}} on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 returned total 7.

Index c's mapped time field is a keyword, so no time filter was applied by the tool and its documents (including ingest_ts values 2026-11-21T08:01:00-09:04:00, later than the authorized window end 2026-11-21T06:58:04Z) cannot be proven to fall inside the authorized window; the 'today' counts rest on the documents' own ingest_ts strings, not on a server-side time filter.

The 16 documents of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 are probably dated outside the authorized window (all queries there returned 0 documents), so its severity values and hence its whole-index ERROR count could not be observed; this is not evidence that the index contains no ERROR entries.

To make index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 queryable in time-bounded searches, ensure its documents carry an in-window @timestamp (or reindex with one); to make app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 time-filterable, map ingest_ts as a date field (currently keyword) instead of relying on lexicographic string ranges.

gaps: Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: no document matched the @timestamp time filter over the full authorized window (2026-11-20T06:58:04Z-2026-11-21T06:58:04Z) even though the index holds 16 documents, and the tool's @timestamp filter cannot be turned off, so the documents' timestamps, their severity values and the whole-index ERROR count are unknown; the in-window reading is 0, not a verified index-wide zero.

Whether index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 uses the value 'ERROR' (exact casing/spelling) for its keyword severity field could not be verified because no document of that index was returned in the authorized window.

Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps no date-typed field (ingest_ts is keyword), so no server-side time filter was applied; its documents, including ingest_ts values 2026-11-21T08:01:00-09:04:00 which are after the authorized window end 06:58:04Z, cannot be proven to belong to the authorized window, and the keyword range is lexicographic rather than date-typed.
'Today' was interpreted as 2026-11-21 UTC, derived from the run reference time 2026-11-21T06:58:04Z; if a different timezone defines 'today' for this data, the index c range bounds would shift.

The severity_num encoding of app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 (5=ERROR, 6=FATAL, 3=INFO) was inferred from the bracketed tags in the msg field of the returned documents, not from a mapping-level or authoritative severity definition.
next_steps: Ask the owner of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 to confirm the intended @timestamp values of its 16 documents, or provide a wider authorized time window, so its severity breakdown can be queried.
Confirm with the app-280 log producer that severity_num 5 means ERROR and 6 means FATAL in index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, since this deviates from syslog numbering where 3 is error.

Recommend remapping ingest_ts in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 to a date field (or adding @timestamp) so time-bounded queries use a real date filter, and standardize the severity field name/value convention across the three indices.
